title: Security Incident Response And Escalation Roadmap
goal: Define and implement a defensive escalation system so Odysseus can detect security anomalies, preserve evidence, diagnose causes, recommend containment, and execute only explicitly allowed remediation actions.
principles: No hackback, no retaliation, no offensive scanning against third-party systems.
Evidence first: preserve redacted facts before remediation changes state.
Read-only diagnostics are allowed by default; mutations require policy and operator confirmation.
Incident mode must fail closed around secrets, private logs and DSGVO-sensitive content.
CrowdSec remediation, firewall changes, restarts, token rotation and deploy rollback are gated actions.

related_roadmaps.relationship: Provides metrics, logs, CrowdSec and Grafana/Loki/Prometheus evidence.
Provides unified event correlation, redacted debug bundles and read-only MCP diagnostics.

incident_ladder.name: watch
incident_ladder.meaning: Low-confidence anomaly such as isolated scanner hits or a small error spike.

incident_ladder.name: alert
incident_ladder.meaning: Repeated suspicious behavior, auth failures, unexpected endpoint probing or subsystem failure with security relevance.

incident_ladder.name: contain
incident_ladder.meaning: Active brute force, exploit signature, abuse pattern, suspicious repeated access or service disruption.
allowed_autonomy: execute pre-approved soft block only if policy allows
incident_ladder.operator_notification: immediate with approve or deny action ids

incident_ladder.name: lockdown
incident_ladder.meaning: Secret leak suspicion, admin-token abuse, data exfiltration suspicion, webshell suspicion or confirmed compromise indicator.
allowed_autonomy: force local-only analysis for sensitive evidence
request explicit operator Go for token rotation, session invalidation, service restart or network isolation

incident_ladder.name: recovery
incident_ladder.meaning: Containment is complete and the system must return to a trusted operating state.

auto_allowed: Telegram or UI notification with redacted facts
confirmation_required: log level increase that may capture private data
never_allowed: doxxing or identity enrichment beyond defensive IP reputation
private log/document upload to external API models while incident or DSGVO mode is active
broad firewall changes without explicit approval

privacy_requirements: No raw IP address in user-facing summary unless operator policy permits it.
No tokens, cookies, authorization headers or raw private documents.
Use hashes or redacted refs for attacker identifiers unless needed for an approved defensive action.

tool_policy: Action execute requires an existing prepared action_id and explicit operator approval.
No direct shell or arbitrary command execution through the incident MCP surface.
No broad firewall, file delete or secret mutation tools in MVP.

safe_parallel_tracks.reason: Model and policy can be developed against a shared contract with separate files.
Classifier output and notification formatting are separable if they share incident object tests.
MCP tools and runbook docs are separable until final integration.

avoid_parallel_tracks.reason: Both touch MCP debug server and tool policy; integrate serially.
Remediation must wait until observability evidence and gates are stable.

slice_queue.goal: Map likely attacker scenarios against Odysseus surfaces and define which evidence source detects each scenario.
slice_queue.done_when: A redacted threat inventory covers SSH, reverse proxy/tunnel, Nextcloud, Odysseus API, Telegram bridge, MCP and provider/secret misuse.
slice_queue.evidence: Created docs/plans/security-incident-threat-inventory.json with redacted defensive scenarios for SSH, reverse proxy/tunnel, Nextcloud, Odysseus API, Telegram bridge, MCP debug surface, provider/secret handling and RaptorGraph/Memory. The inventory maps evidence sources, initial escalation levels, auto-allowed actions, confirmation-required actions and never-allowed actions without real identifiers or private content.

slice_queue.goal: Implement the incident object, action object and escalation ladder as backend models.
slice_queue.done_when: Incidents and recommended actions serialize safely, reject forbidden fields and enforce severity/level constraints.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented src/security_incident_model.py with redacted incident and recommended-action builders, escalation levels 0-5, severity/status constraints, confidence validation, confirmation-required remediation action policy, never-allowed action rejection, sensitive evidence hashing and compact incident summaries. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 8 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Implement the response policy engine that decides observe, diagnose, recommend or act based on severity, confidence and approved gates.
slice_queue.done_when: The policy engine auto-allows only read-only diagnostics and debug bundles, requires confirmation for remediation, and blocks never-allowed actions.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented src/security_response_policy.py with prepare-only action decisions, incident response aggregation, policy readiness, read-only auto-allow decisions, remediation gate requirements, confidence/level blockers, never-allowed denial, incident/DSGVO mode sensitive-action blocking, and no live execution path. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 16 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Build initial anomaly classifiers over unified events and observability summaries.
slice_queue.done_when: Classifier can identify repeated auth failures, suspicious endpoint probing, Telegram abuse, service-down security events and secret-leak indicators from redacted events.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented src/security_anomaly_classifier.py with deterministic anomaly families for repeated auth failures, endpoint probing, Telegram abuse/spam patterns, service-down security events and secret-leak indicators using only redacted runtime event fields and observability counters. It returns SecurityIncident candidates with read-only/gated recommended actions and rejects raw-content or secret-marked inputs. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 13 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Create redacted incident notification formats for Telegram and future UI without exposing sensitive evidence.
slice_queue.done_when: Operator receives concise incident summaries, action IDs and approve/deny instructions without raw secrets or private content.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented src/security_incident_notifications.py with prepare-only redacted incident notification payloads for Telegram and future UI, compact action summaries, approve/deny command hints, debug bundle references and no delivery target handling. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 89 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Expose read-only incident response tools through the MCP debug workbench and define gated action tools without enabling live remediation by default.
slice_queue.done_when: MCP can list/read/trace incidents and prepare recommendations, while execute remains gated and policy-controlled.
slice_queue.evidence: Extended mcp_servers/debug_server.py with read-only security_incident_list/read/trace, security_recent_anomalies, security_policy_readiness, security_recommend_next_action, security_debug_bundle_read and gated action stubs. security_action_execute remains blocked without an action store/gate and all tools report writes_performed=false. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 23 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Write defensive runbooks for common incident types and recovery flow.
slice_queue.done_when: Runbooks define observe, diagnose, contain, lockdown and recovery steps with clear operator gates.
slice_queue.evidence: Added defensive runbooks for security incident response, CrowdSec prepare-only remediation and Telegram operator incident notifications. The runbooks define observe/diagnose/contain/lockdown/recovery flow, redaction rules, approve/deny semantics, and live gates without enabling remediation.

slice_queue.goal: Implement safe preparation of remediation actions without executing live changes.
slice_queue.done_when: Odysseus can prepare redacted action plans for CrowdSec temp block, restart request, scheduler pause/retry and token-rotation prep, but cannot execute them without a live gate.
slice_queue.evidence: Implemented src/security_remediation_actions.py with prepare-only remediation plans for CrowdSec, service restart, scheduler, RaptorGraph, Nextcloud retry, token/session, Cloudflare, deploy rollback and log-level actions. Plans stay dry_run, writes_performed=false and allowed_to_execute=false even when gates are approved. Focused tests passed on 2026-07-03: 13 passed, 1 warning.

slice_queue.goal: Run a tabletop live smoke using synthetic/redacted events to verify incident creation, notification, MCP diagnosis and approve/deny flow.
slice_queue.done_when: A synthetic incident escalates to alert, produces a debug bundle, notifies the operator and records an approve/deny decision without touching firewall, CrowdSec or live services.

gate_queue.decision_needed: Approve a synthetic incident tabletop smoke with no real remediation.
gate_queue.risk_if_bypassed: Even synthetic notifications can confuse operators if not clearly marked.

gate_queue.decision_needed: Approve whether Odysseus may execute CrowdSec temporary bans and under what confidence/severity thresholds.
gate_queue.risk_if_bypassed: False positives could block legitimate operator access.

gate_queue.decision_needed: Decide which lockdown actions, if any, Odysseus may take automatically.
gate_queue.risk_if_bypassed: Over-broad lockdown could interrupt legitimate operations or hide evidence.

definition_of_done: Security anomalies are represented as structured incidents with severity, confidence, evidence and recommended actions.
Odysseus can diagnose incidents using unified events and read-only MCP tools.
Operator notifications are precise and redacted.
Remediation is policy-gated and never defaults to arbitrary shell, firewall or CrowdSec mutation.
A synthetic tabletop exercise proves escalation, debug bundle creation and approve/deny flow.

recommended_next_action.reason: SIR-0 through SIR-7 are complete; the remaining SIR slice is live-gated synthetic tabletop validation.
